description: The chart illustrates measured “effect” values across language families for six model–layer combinations, shown as grouped bars with error bars. The horizontal axis lists the categorical language families in left-to-right order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with the axis label “family.” The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale with visible tick marks at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30, spanning roughly from slightly below 0 to the mid-30s; each bar includes a vertical error bar with caps. For each family, six adjacent bars appear in the legend order and colors: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). IE-Baltic shows small positive bars (about 1–6) with mBERT-B₂ around ~6 and XLM-B₂ around ~5; IE-Germanic shows mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ near ~10, mBERT-R₂ slightly below 0, XLM-R₂ near 0, and both B₂ bars around ~15. IE-Indic has the tallest cluster overall, with mBERT-R₂ around ~20, XLM-R₂ around ~18, mBERT-B₂ around ~24, and XLM-B₂ around ~21, while the L₂ bars are near 0. IE-Romance shows mid-range values with mBERT-L₂ around ~6, XLM-L₂ around ~4, mBERT-R₂ around ~5, XLM-R₂ around ~1, mBERT-B₂ around ~12–13, and XLM-B₂ around ~6. IE-Slavic shows mBERT-L₂ around ~10–11 and XLM-L₂ around ~9, R₂ bars near ~1 and ~0, and B₂ bars around ~17 (mBERT-B₂) and ~15–16 (XLM-B₂). IE-other shows L₂ bars around ~6, R₂ bars near 0, and B₂ bars around ~8. Isolate shows values close to 0 for L₂ and small positive values for R₂ and B₂ (roughly ~1–2). Semitic shows larger L₂ and B₂ values, with mBERT-L₂ around ~11, XLM-L₂ around ~16, mBERT-R₂ around ~−2, XLM-R₂ around ~−1, mBERT-B₂ around ~15, and XLM-B₂ around ~19–20, with notably large error bars on several Semitic bars. Uralic shows very small positive values near ~0–2 across all six bars. The bars are not visually sorted by height; they follow the fixed family order on the x-axis, and no individual bars appear specially highlighted beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars.
